battle.name: 中非內戰
battle.brief: 維基百科戰爭列表所列的中非內戰於2004年3月在中非共和國爆發，軍隊叛變與武裝衝突交錯，班吉及北部地區受到影響，地方安全與政府控制受到挑戰。加特林機槍（正式型號為Gatling gun）的服役年為1860年，早於本場衝突，是美國地面部隊曾列裝的真實機槍。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 加特林機槍屬美國陸軍早期制式重機槍，配置於步兵與火力支援單位，定位為持續射擊的壓制武器，屬地面作戰裝備體系。

countries: 中非共和國是唯一的主戰場：班吉市內的軍營、總統府街區、法軍作戰分隊的臨時據點，以及西北部奧姆貝拉－姆波科省以博桑瓜為中心的公路走廊與鑽石開採區，都構成實際戰線。法國以「仁慈行動」（Opération Miséricorde）名義派兵干預，之後轉為以班吉姆波科國際機場、總統府與跑道為核心的保護性駐軍。剛果共和國（布拉柴維爾）是帕塔塞出逃後的駐地，也是科林巴武裝人員與武器裝備流入的方向；喀麥隆、查德與剛果民主共和國只提供邊境通行、情報交換與偶爾的後勤轉運，並未投入地面部隊。叛軍方除了科林巴的私人武裝，還包括班吉各營區因欠薪而騷動的現役軍人，以及北部已先行脫隊、拒絕復編的地方武裝。
countriesEn: The Central African Republic was the only main battlefield: the barracks and presidential palace districts of Bangui, the temporary forward positions of the French detachments, and the road corridor and diamond-mining area around Bossangoa in Ombella-M'Poko prefecture in the northwest all formed the actual fighting lines. France intervened under the name Operation Miséricorde, then shifted into a protective posture centred on Bangui M'Poko International Airport, the presidential palace and the runway. The Republic of Congo, at Brazzaville, was where Patassé went into exile and the direction from which Kolingba's fighters and weapons flowed; Cameroon, Chad and the Democratic Republic of the Congo provided only border transit, intelligence exchange and occasional logistics, with no ground forces committed. On the insurgent side, besides Kolingba's private armed group, were serving soldiers in Bangui's barracks agitated by unpaid salaries and armed groups in the north that had already broken from their units and refused demobilisation.
people: François Bozizé, formerly commander of the national defence and security forces, led the coup that deposed Patassé on 13 March 2003 and took control of the military; he later won a majority in the December 2003 presidential election. The deposed Ange-Félix Patassé was flown out on a French military aircraft to Brazzaville and remained in exile. André Kolingba, president from 1993 to 1999 and a defeated candidate in the 2003 election, was the initiator and supreme commander of the May 2004 rising, personally crossing from Brazzaville into the country with, according to reporting, only a few dozen armed men. Nicolas Tiangaye served as prime minister and liaised with the army command; Abel Goumba, one of the principal opposition figures, shuttled between exile and the interior and kept attacking the conduct of the election and the restructuring of the armed forces. On the French side a commander from the Middle African theatre headquarters led the deployed detachments, his name given inconsistently in public briefings. In the local command were the officers of the presidential guard and the gendarmerie, and the NCOs and junior officers in the Bangui barracks who had gone unpaid.
peopleEn: François Bozizé, formerly chief of the national defence and security forces, led the coup that overthrew Patassé on 13 March 2003 and seized the army; he would later win a majority in the December 2003 presidential election. The deposed Ange-Félix Patassé was carried out on a French military aircraft to Brazzaville and stayed in exile. André Kolingba, president from 1993 to 1999 and a defeated candidate in the 2003 poll, initiated and personally commanded the May 2004 rising, crossing from Brazzaville into the country with, according to reporting, only a few dozen armed men. Nicolas Tiangaye served as prime minister and maintained contact with the army command; Abel Goumba, one of the leading opposition figures, moved between exile and the interior and repeatedly attacked the election and the restructuring of the forces. For France, a commander dispatched by the Middle African headquarters led the ground detachments, his name reported inconsistently across official briefings. On the local side stood the officers of the presidential guard and the gendarmerie, together with the NCOs and junior officers of the Bangui barracks who had not been paid.
kits: 法軍分隊以 FAMAS F1 突擊步槍、MAS 49 自動步槍、MAA 52（FN MAG 系列）中通用機槍、VAB 裝甲運兵車與卡車為主，配屬便攜式無線電、直升機與野戰醫療組，彈藥口徑為 5.56×45 毫米與 7.62×51 毫米。中非軍與叛軍主力則是蘇聯 AK-47、AKM、AK-74，以及 1980 年代以後陸續交付的中國 56 式步槍與 56 式班用機槍，輕機槍為 PKM 與 RPK，重機槍有 NSV（果魯諾夫）固定在改裝皮卡與土製技術車上；反裝甲武器為 RPG-7 與 81／82 毫米迫擊砲，手雷為 F-1 與 RGD-5，手槍多為 PM 馬卡洛夫。車輛以豐田 Land Cruiser 技術車與卡車為主。彈藥、柴油與電池長期短缺，7.62×39 毫米與 7.62×54 毫米彈種無法互通補充，法軍的北約口徑與中非口徑完全不能合用，後勤必須分兩套帳冊計算，軍需品只能以飛機與小批量車隊輸送。
kitsEn: The French detachments fielded FAMAS F1 assault rifles, MAS 49 self-loading rifles, MAA 52 general-purpose machine guns (FN MAG family), VAB armoured personnel carriers and trucks, supported by portable radios, helicopters and field medical sections, with 5.56×45 mm and 7.62×51 mm ammunition. The Central African army and the insurgents relied chiefly on Soviet AK-47, AKM and AK-74 rifles, plus Chinese Type 56 rifles and Type 56 general-purpose machine guns delivered from the 1980s onward, with PKM and RPK light machine guns and NSV (Goryunov) heavy machine guns bolted to modified pickups and improvised technicals. Anti-armour weapons were RPG-7 and 81/82 mm mortars; grenades were F-1 and RGD-5; sidearms were mostly PM Makarov pistols. Vehicles were chiefly Toyota Land Cruiser technicals and trucks. Ammunition, diesel and batteries were chronically short, 7.62×39 mm and 7.62×54 mm ammunition could not be exchanged or pooled, and the French NATO calibres were entirely incompatible with local weapons, so logistics had to be run on two separate accounting systems and supplies moved by air and in small truck convoys.
tactics: 3 月的兵變接近自發性營變：幾個班排在領餉與換班時同時嘩變，先搶占營區軍械庫、剪斷通往總統府的通信線，再以路障與散兵在班吉幾條主要街道布防，用 RPG-7 與迫擊砲對付低空掠過的直升機與裝甲車，白晝避免在開闊地集中，夜間則靠近對方巡邏路線設伏。從可查的交戰記錄可見的做法與此相符。法軍的對策是先以機場、油料庫與通往總統府的道路連成外圈檢查站，用裝甲運兵車封住街口，在市區內避免使用重火力以免誤擊，並由直升機巡飛、頻繁換位的小分隊攜軍醫與通譯進駐；數次會議後同意讓法軍撤出市區，只保留機場與總統府周圍的保護分隊。5 月科林巴起兵時，先以數輛汽車組成快速車隊沿班吉至博桑瓜約三百公里的公路北上，占領博桑瓜並切斷通往南部礦區的道路；政府軍先封路斷糧，再以晝間推進、夜間宿營交替的方式逐點清剿，叛軍在失去車輛與無線電後化整為零，藏入礦場與村落，最後在城外公路被截斷退路而崩潰。
tacticsEn: The March mutiny followed the pattern of an spontaneous barracks rising: several platoons revolted simultaneously while drawing pay and changing the guard, first seizing armoury depots and cutting the communications lines to the presidential palace, then laying roadblocks and deploying skirmishers along the main streets of Bangui, engaging low-flying helicopters and armoured vehicles with RPG-7s and mortars, avoiding concentration in the open by day and lying in wait close to enemy patrol routes at night. What the surviving accounts describe matches that pattern. The French answer was to string outer checkpoint rings around the airport, the fuel depot and the roads to the presidential palace, sealing street mouths with armoured personnel carriers, withholding heavy fire inside the town to avoid misidentification, and flying helicopter patrols while small, frequently relocated squads carrying medics and interpreters moved forward. After several meetings the French agreed to leave the city proper and keep only protective detachments around the airport and the palace. When Kolingba rose in May, a fast column of cars moved north along the roughly three-hundred-kilometre road from Bangui to Bossangoa, seized the town and cut the routes to the southern mining areas. Government forces first closed the roads to strangle the column, then worked point by point with daytime pushes alternating with night bivouacs; once the insurgents lost their vehicles and radios they dispersed into the mines and villages, and were broken when their withdrawal on the road out of town was cut off.
data: 可核對的時間節點如下：2003 年 3 月 13 日博齊澤部在班吉發動政變，帕塔塞被送上法軍飛機撤往布拉柴維爾；3 月 15 日班吉的卡薩營區與羅什營區爆發欠薪兵變，至 16 日法軍以「仁慈行動」落地接管機場與主要路口，17 至 19 日市區零星交火持續，叛變並蔓延到貝爾貝拉蒂、博桑瓜等外圍營區；4 月初兵變人員接受復編與追補津貼，法軍於 4 月撤出班吉市區；2003 年 12 月上旬舉行總統大選，博齊澤得到約五成一票的支持。2004 年 5 月 18 日科林巴部占領博桑瓜，5 月 20 日政府軍奪回該鎮，5 月 21 日科林巴投降，其後數週獲赦並被任命為使節。兵力與地理方面，中非武裝部隊總數（含憲兵）估計六千至八千人，憲兵約四千人，班吉駐軍與總統警衛合計逾一千人；法軍首批落地人數各報導介於二百至三百五十人之間。中非人口約四百萬，班吉約六十萬；班吉至博桑瓜公路距離約三百公里，途中檢查站由政府軍與地方武裝共同把守，無線電通訊在衝突期間多靠隨軍便攜台與衛星電話，軍需品只能以飛機與車隊小批量輸送。
dataEn: The verifiable timeline runs as follows. On 13 March 2003 Bozizé's troops staged the coup in Bangui and Patassé was put on a French aircraft and flown to Brazzaville. On 15 March the mutiny broke out in the Kassa and Roche barracks of Bangui; by the 16th French troops under Operation Miséricorde had landed and taken the airport and the main junctions, intermittent street fighting continued from the 17th to the 19th, and the revolt spread to outlying garrisons such as Berbérati and Bossangoa. In early April the mutineers were accepted back into units with arrears paid, and the French withdrew from the city proper during April. A presidential election was held in the first third of December 2003, in which Bozizé took support of about fifty-one per cent. On 18 May 2004 Kolingba's men seized Bossangoa; government forces retook the town on the 20th; Kolingba surrendered on the 21st, and within weeks was pardoned and appointed to a diplomatic post. On strength and geography: the armed forces, gendarmerie included, are estimated at six to eight thousand, with roughly four thousand gendarmes and more than a thousand combining the Bangui garrison and the presidential guard; French reports put the initial landing between two hundred and three hundred and fifty men. The population stands at about four million, Bangui at around six hundred thousand; the road from Bangui to Bossangoa runs about three hundred kilometres, with checkpoints held jointly by government troops and local armed groups, radio traffic carried largely on portable sets and satellite telephones, and supplies moving only by air and in small convoys.
cause: 兵變的直接原因是薪餉與口糧制度。軍人的薪資被拖欠數月，憲兵的薪資由法軍代為發放，而外界普遍認為導火線之一是政府以命令取消了所謂「孔多馬」（kondoma）的慣例：「孔多馬」指每日軍用口糧配給，過去軍人可攜配給離營變賣貼補家用，此禁令等於切斷許多基層軍人的額外收入；具體比重各方說法不一。制度層面上，1996 至 2003 年內戰的善後、復員與賠償從未真正完成，退伍與復編未果者滯留營區，成為騷動的溫床；軍中藥品與燃料不足、軍官與士兵待遇差距被公開化，也加深了對立。2004 年科林巴起兵則疊加在 12 月大選的爭議、反對派對結果的抵制，以及鑽石特許權與礦區收入流向班吉政府的權力網絡之上；科林巴與博齊澤同樣出自奧姆貝拉－姆波科省，起兵因此帶有地方政治與資源分配色彩，而不只是選舉抗議。
causeEn: The proximate causes of the mutiny lay in pay and rations. Soldiers' salaries were months in arrears, gendarmerie pay was being paid directly by the French, and the wider view held that one trigger was a government decree abolishing the kondoma custom: kondoma referred to the daily military ration, which soldiers had traditionally been allowed to carry out of barracks and sell to supplement their income, and banning it cut off that supplementary revenue for many rank-and-file men, though accounts differ on its precise weight. Structurally, the demobilisation, reintegration and compensation promised after the 1996–2003 civil war were never completed, so demobilised and unreintegrated men remained in barracks as a breeding ground for unrest; shortages of medicines and fuel in the units, and the open gap in treatment between officers and enlisted men, deepened the grievance. Kolingba's rising in 2004 sat on top of the contested December election, the opposition boycott of its result, and the network that channelled diamond concessions and mining revenue towards the Bangui government. Kolingba and Bozizé both came from Ombella-M'Poko prefecture, which gave the rising the character of local politics and of a struggle over the distribution of resources, not merely an electoral protest.
impact: 最直接的後果是主權與軍隊的重新編排：法軍由干預者轉為保護者，撤出班吉市區後只留少量分隊看守機場、總統府與跑道，經費由中非財政支付，國家預算因而被安全支出與外幣結算長期牽動；兵變人員被分成接受復編、晉升與補發薪資，以及拒絕解散武裝另尋出路兩類，前者在軍中形成新的忠于博齊澤的派系，後者則在北部與西部山區留下帶槍小團體，成為往後擴大事端的骨幹。政治面，反對派在軍隊與行政體系中的空間被壓縮，總統權力因軍隊整編而集中，國家預算、鑽石收益與軍餉三者的矛盾未被解決，國際社會亦未派駐正式維和部隊。地緣面，因 5 月的戰事被迅速壓平，2004 年下半年中非避免了進一步的全面內戰，但把矛盾累積到下一次危機。
impactEn: The most direct consequence was a reordering of sovereignty and of the army. The French moved from intervener to protector: after leaving central Bangui they kept only small detachments guarding the airport, the presidential palace and the runway, at a cost met by the Central African treasury, so national budgets stayed tied to security spending and foreign-currency settlements for years. The mutineers split into those accepted back into units with promotion and back pay, and those refusing to disband and looking for another path. The first group formed a new faction loyal to Bozizé inside the forces; the second left armed bands in the northern and western highlands that later served as the backbone of larger eruptions. Politically, the opposition's room inside the army and the administration was compressed, presidential power concentrated as the forces were reorganised, and the contradiction between the state budget, diamond revenue and military pay remained unresolved. No formal United Nations peacekeeping force was deployed. Geographically, because the May fighting was crushed quickly, the Central African Republic avoided a wider civil war in the second half of 2004, but the contradictions were carried forward to the next crisis.
result: 結果是政府方的全面勝利，但代價被推到未來。2003 年 3 月的兵變被壓制，帕塔塞流亡國外，博齊澤以軍事與選舉兩種手段坐實權位；2004 年 5 月科林巴的武裝起兵僅維持數日，博桑瓜於 20 日被政府軍奪回，科林巴於 21 日投降，之後獲赦並被安排到外交或顧問性質的位置，其追隨者或被收編、或散入鑽石礦區。到 2004 年底，班吉與各省的主要道路由政府軍巡邏隊控制，博桑瓜與礦區恢復有限度的官方管理，法軍仍以保護隊形式駐紮機場與總統府，中非軍隊的忠誠度則高度依賴薪資與裝備是否準時發放。留下來的問題十分具體：欠薪與配給制度未改、復編完成的標準不明、鑽石收益的稽核薄弱，以及一支規模不大但分布廣的武裝後備力量；任何一次新的薪資斷裂或首都權力轉移，都可能讓同一套條件再度爆發。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete government victory, with the cost deferred. The March 2003 mutiny was suppressed, Patassé went into exile, and Bozizé confirmed his position by two means, military and electoral. Kolingba's armed rising of May 2004 lasted only days: Bossangoa was retaken by government forces on the 20th, Kolingba surrendered on the 21st, and he was then pardoned and placed in a diplomatic or advisory role, while some followers were taken into units and others scattered into the diamond areas. By the end of 2004 the main roads of Bangui and the provinces were covered by government patrols, Bossangoa and the mining zone returned to limited official administration, the French remained at the airport and the presidential palace as a protective force, and the loyalty of the Central African forces depended heavily on whether pay and equipment arrived on time. What was left behind was concrete: an unchanged system of arrears and rations, no clear definition of what counted as completed reintegration, weak auditing of diamond revenue, and a small but widely distributed armed reserve. Any new rupture in pay, or any transfer of power in the capital, could make the same set of conditions detonate again.
